data.title: S&P Revises Outlook on French Credit Rating to Negative From Stable — WSJ
data.description:
By Don Nico Forbes

France's credit outlook was revised to negative from stable by S&P Global Ratings on Friday, paving the way for a rating downgrade as mounting public debt and political uncertainty threaten to undermine efforts to bring the country's finances under control.

France's credit rating was affirmed at A+, but the outlook change signals that S&P sees a greater risk of a downgrade in the coming months if France fails to make progress on reducing its budget deficit and stabilizing its debt burden.

"The negative outlook on France reflects rising government debt against a backdrop of subdued economic growth prospects amid weak political consensus on how to tackle the large underlying budget deficit," S&P said in a statement.

Earlier Friday, France's statistics agency published revised figures that showed the economy entered a recession in the three months through September, with output contracting in both the second and third quarters.

The S&P decision comes as France faces a difficult budget negotiation for 2027, with the government struggling to secure parliamentary backing for measures to reduce the budget deficit. The government is targeting a deficit of 5% next year, but the European Commission forecasts 5.4%.

S&P's decision leaves France with an A+ rating, one notch below its previous AA- rating following a cut in 2025. This leaves the country rated alongside Spain, Portugal and Japan, but below Germany, the U.K. and Belgium, reflecting the deterioration of its fiscal position in recent years.

France's borrowing costs have remained elevated amid investor concerns about the country's fiscal outlook. The yield on France's 10-year government bond stood at around 4.75% on Thursday, while the spread over German bonds was around 1.5 percentage points, after peaking at over 1.7 percentage points earlier this autumn.

The S&P move follows Moody's decision last month to maintain France's rating at Aa3, with a negative outlook, while Fitch revised its outlook on France to negative last month, affirming its rating at A+. An A+ is one grade below Aa3 on the agencies' respective scales.

France's political turmoil has complicated efforts to tackle its fiscal problems since the 2024 snap election left no party with a parliamentary majority, making it difficult for successive governments to secure approval for budgets or advance spending cuts and tax reforms.

The uncertainty is unlikely to dissipate ahead of the 2027 presidential race, with investors questioning whether the next administration will have the political backing to curb borrowing. The prospect of policies proposed by polling front-runner Marine Le Pen on the far right, as well as Jean-Luc Melenchon on the left, has added to concerns about the country's fiscal trajectory.

Write to Don Nico Forbes at don.forbes@wsj.com

data.title: GoGo AI Announces Effective Date of Share Consolidation
data.description:
VANCOUVER, British Columbia, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- GoGo AI Network Inc. FSE:4E9 (“GoGo” or the “Company”) announces that, further to its news release on November 16, 2026, it will consolidate the common shares of the Company (each, a “Share”) on the basis of one (1) post-consolidation Share for every ten (10) pre-consolidation Shares (the “Consolidation”). The Shares are expected to commence trading on a post-consolidation basis at the opening of the market on December 3, 2026. There is no name change or stock symbol change in connection with the Consolidation. The new CUSIP is 379973209 ISIN:CA3799732092.

The Company currently has 113,819,555 Shares issued and outstanding. Following the Consolidation, approximately 11,381,955 Shares, subject to adjustments for rounding, will be issued and outstanding. No fractional Shares will be issued in connection with the Consolidation, and any fractional Share resulting from the Consolidation will be rounded down to the nearest whole Share.

Endeavor Trust Corporation will mail out a Letter of Transmittal to the shareholders of record on December 3, 2026, providing instructions on exchanging pre-Consolidation share certificates for post-Consolidation share certificates. Shareholders are encouraged to send their share certificates, together with their Letter of Transmittal, to Endeavor in accordance with the instructions in the Letter of Transmittal.

Shareholders who hold their Shares through a broker, investment dealer, bank, trust company or other intermediary are not required to take any action.

GoGo AI Network Inc. is an investment issuer focused on identifying, investing in, and supporting early-stage and growth-stage companies developing artificial intelligence, automation, and next-generation software technologies. data.title: Apple May Consider Ceramic Design For 20th-Anniversary IPhone
data.description:
CUPERTINO (dpa-AFX) - Apple Inc. (AAPL) may be exploring ceramic components for its 20th-anniversary iPhone, expected to launch in 2027, according to recent leaks. The reports suggest the company could be considering a limited-edition model featuring ceramic elements, although the details remain unclear.

Leaker Fixed Focus Digital says it has seen ceramic components for next year's flagship iPhone, while another source notes that production capacity may be limited. The project could advance to mass production if it passes engineering validation, though it's unclear whether ceramic will be used for the rear panel, main enclosure, or smaller exterior parts.

Some speculation may stem from confusion with Apple's existing Ceramic Shield technology. The 2027 anniversary models are also expected to feature a major glass-focused redesign and a quad-curved display. Apple has not confirmed these reports or its plans for the device.

data.title: Yukon Metals Announces C$5.25M Private Placement
data.description:
NOT FOR DISTRIBUTION TO UNITED STATES NEWSWIRE SERVICES OR FOR DISSEMINATION IN THE UNITED STATES. NOT AN OFFER OF SECURITIES FOR SALE IN THE UNITED STATES

VANCOUVER, British Columbia, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Yukon Metals Corp. (CSE: YMC, FSE: E770, OTCQB: YMMCF) (“Yukon Metals” or the “Company”) is pleased to announce a fully subscribed and allocated non-brokered private placement (the “Offering”) of up to 25,609,756 flow-through units of the Company (each, a “FT Unit”) at a price of $0.205 per FT Unit, for aggregate gross proceeds of up to $5,250,000 (the “Proceeds”).

Each FT Unit will consist of one common share of the Company (each, a “Common Share”), to be issued as a “flow-through share” within the meaning of subsection 66(15) of the Income Tax Act (Canada) (the “Tax Act”), and one-half of one common share purchase warrant (each whole warrant, a “Warrant”), with each Warrant to be issued on a non-flow-through basis.

Each Warrant will entitle the holder thereof to purchase one Common Share at a price of $0.30 for a period of two years following the closing date of the Offering. For the avoidance of doubt, neither the Warrants nor the Common Shares issuable upon exercise of the Warrants will qualify as “flow-through shares” for purposes of the Tax Act.

The Company, pursuant to the provisions of the Tax Act, shall use an amount equal to the Proceeds to incur eligible “Canadian exploration expenses” that qualify as “flow-through critical mineral mining expenditures”, each as defined in the Tax Act (the “Qualifying Expenditures”), on the Company’s AZ copper project. The Company shall renounce the Qualifying Expenditures to subscribers of the FT Units effective on or before December 31, 2026.

The FT Units will be offered by way of private placement pursuant to available exemptions from the prospectus requirements under National Instrument 45-106 – Prospectus Exemptions. All securities issued in connection with the Offering will be subject to a hold period of four months and one day from the closing date of the Offering in accordance with applicable Canadian securities laws.

In connection with the Offering, the Company may pay finder's fees of up to 6% of the proceeds from subscribers introduced by eligible finders in cash and issue finder’s warrants equal to up to 6% of the proceeds from subscribers introduced by eligible finders.

The Offering is expected to close on or about December 10, 2026, or on such other date as the Company may determine. Completion of the Offering is subject to customary conditions, including, but not limited to, the receipt of all necessary regulatory approvals, inclusive of (if applicable) the approval of the Canadian Securities Exchange.

The FT Units described herein have not been and will not be registered under the United States Securities Act of 1933, as amended, or any U.S. state securities laws, and may not be offered or sold in the United States absent registration or available exemptions from such registration requirements.

This news release does not constitute an offer to acquire securities in any jurisdiction.

About Yukon Metals Corp.

Yukon Metals is well financed and represents a property portfolio built on over 30 years of prospecting by the Berdahl family, the prospecting team behind Snowline Gold Corp.’s portfolio of primary gold assets. The Yukon Metals portfolio consists primarily of copper-gold and silver-lead-zinc assets, with a substantial tungsten, gold and silver component. The Company is led by an experienced Board of Directors and Management team across technical and finance disciplines.

Yukon Metals is focused on fostering sustainable growth and prosperity within Yukon's local communities, while simultaneously enhancing stakeholder value. The Company’s strategy centers around inclusivity and shared prosperity, offering both community members and investors the chance to contribute to, and benefit from, its ventures.

The Yukon

The Yukon Territory is an underexplored and minerally endowed district with a mining history dating back to the Klondike Gold Rush of 1898. With a progressive permitting regime, geopolitical stability and supportive government, it is well positioned to foster the next generation of mines. The Yukon is host to a highly experienced and conscientious local workforce, fostered by a long culture of exploration coupled with deep respect for the land. Recent major discoveries with local roots such as Snowline Gold Corp.’s Rogue Project - Valley Discovery, demonstrate the Yukon’s potential to generate fresh district-scale mining opportunities.

data.title: The Fresh Factory Reports Q3 2026 Billed Revenue of $15.0 Million, Up 28%, and EBITDA Growth of 58% Year Over Year
data.description:
Key points:
  • The Company reported a record quarterly billed revenue of $15.0M (CAD $21.4M) in Q3 2026, representing a YoY increase of 28% from Q3 2025.
  • The Company achieved positive EBITDA of $0.60M (CAD $0.85M) and adjusted EBITDA of $0.75M (CAD $1.06M) in Q3 2026, the Company's strongest adjusted EBITDA since Q2 2025.
  • Q3 2026 was the Company's first full quarter operating solely from its Bolingbrook and Downers Grove facilities, which together total approximately 210,000 square feet.
  • The Company received a capital grant totalling $765,000 (CAD $1.09M) from the Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity (DCEO) under the Business Attraction Prime Sites program.
  • Mitsubishi HC Capital America, Inc. has increased the funds available under the Company's existing asset-based credit facility from US$5 million (CAD $7.1M) to US$7 million (CAD $10.0M).

DOWNERS GROVE, IL / ACCESS Newswire / November 27, 2026 / The Fresh Factory B.C. Ltd. (FRA:Q4Z) ("The Fresh Factory" or the "Company"), a mission-driven company for fresh, clean-label, and better-for-you food and beverage brands, is pleased to announce financial results for the thirteen- and thirty-nine-week periods ending October 3, 2026 ("Q3 2026").

"This was our first full quarter operating exclusively from Bolingbrook and Downers Grove," said Bill Besenhofer, CEO and co-founder of The Fresh Factory. "We delivered record billed revenue of $15.0 million, up 28% year-over-year, while improving adjusted EBITDA for the second consecutive quarter. With our facility consolidation now behind us, we're beginning to see the benefits of a more efficient operating structure. As we continue to bring additional volume into our facilities, we believe we're positioned to generate greater operating leverage and improve profitability."

Financial and Operational Highlights: Q3 2026 vs. Q3 2025

  • Record billed revenue of $15.0M (CAD $21.4M) in Q3 2026 vs. $11.7M (CAD $16.7M) in Q3 2025, a 28% increase, mainly driven by sales to existing strategic partners across a variety of categories, as well as sales to new accounts.
  • Adjusted EBITDA of $0.75M (CAD $1.06M) in Q3 2026 vs. $0.66M (CAD $0.94M) in Q3 2025, a 13% increase and the second consecutive quarterly improvement, as the Company operated its first full quarter from the consolidated Bolingbrook and Downers Grove footprint.
  • The Company reported a net loss of $0.74M (CAD $1.05M) in Q3 2026, compared to a net loss of $0.34M (CAD $0.48M) in Q3 2025, primarily driven by higher depreciation on the Bolingbrook buildout and higher interest expense.
  • Adjusted gross margin was $4.71M (CAD $6.73M) in Q3 2026, compared to $4.11M (CAD $5.87M) in Q3 2025. Adjusted gross margin, as a percentage, was 31% in Q3 2026 vs. 35% in Q3 2025, and improved sequentially from 30% in Q2 2026 as Bolingbrook ramp-up inefficiencies began to subside.

Strategic Areas of Focus

The Fresh Factory is building a platform to serve emerging food and beverage brands in the fresh-food sector with an emphasis on better-for-you products. The Company has established the following three key areas of focus on which it will report on a quarterly basis moving forward.

Execution: Focus on safety, high-quality operations, and strong margins.

  • Adjusted gross margin was $4.71M (CAD $6.73M) for Q3 2026, compared to $4.11M (CAD $5.87M) for Q3 2025.
  • Adjusted gross margin, as a percentage, was 31% for Q3 2026 vs. 35% for Q3 2025, driven by a combination of product-mix changes and Bolingbrook ramp-up costs.
  • Operating profit on a dollar basis was $1.28M (CAD $1.83M) for Q3 2026, compared to $1.44M (CAD $2.06M) for Q3 2025.
  • Operating profit, as a percentage, was 8.5% in Q3 2026 vs. 12.3% in Q3 2025. The margin compression reflects the higher facility and utility costs of the Bolingbrook facility, which carries a substantially larger footprint than the legacy Carol Stream site it replaced. Management expects these dynamics to recede as production volumes build at the consolidated footprint.
  • The Company achieved EBITDA of $0.60M (CAD $0.85M) in Q3 2026.

Growth: Invest in and grow with the right brands across diversified channels.

  • Billed revenue for Q3 2026 was $15.0M (CAD $21.4M), compared to $11.7M (CAD $16.7M) in Q3 2025.
  • The Company's Q3 2026 billed revenue grew 28% YoY, driven by increased demand from existing strategic partners across a variety of categories, as well as sales to new accounts.
  • The Company produced 18.7M packaged units in Q3 2026, compared to 14.6M in Q2 2026, a 28% increase.
  • Q3 2026 was the Company's first full quarter operating from two manufacturing facilities in Bolingbrook and Downers Grove, Illinois, totaling approximately 210,000 square feet, following the exit from the legacy Carol Stream facility on April 30, 2026. The consolidated footprint provides enhanced scale and flexibility to support partners as they grow.
  • The Company received a capital grant totalling $765,000 (CAD $1.09M) from the Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity (DCEO) under the Business Attraction Prime Sites program. The non-dilutive grant supports the Company's ongoing expansion of Illinois manufacturing operations, including the relocation of production to Bolingbrook and improvements to its Downers Grove facility, together with the associated capital investment and creation of new jobs in the state.
  • Mitsubishi HC Capital America, Inc. (the "Lender") has increased the funds available under the Company's existing asset-based credit facility (the "Facility") from US$5 million to US$7 million. The Facility was originally established in September 2025 in the principal amount of US$4 million and increased to US$5 million in December 2025. Funds drawn on the Facility will bear interest at prime plus 1.00% per annum, payable monthly. In connection with the increase, the Facility's borrowing base has been expanded to include a machinery and equipment component, in addition to eligible accounts receivable, and the permitted use of proceeds now includes equipment purchases in addition to working capital and general corporate purposes. The maturity date of the Facility remains as at September 2028. The Company expects that future revenue generated through operations will be sufficient to service and fully repay the Facility on or before its maturity date. A commitment fee of US$30,000 was paid to the Lender in connection with the amendment to the Facility, and a service fee equal to 0.375% of the maximum commitment under the Facility shall be payable on the annual anniversary of the amended Facility.

"This increase gives us more room to fund working capital and to invest in the equipment that supports our customers' growth," said Bill Besenhofer, Chief Executive Officer and Co-Founder of The Fresh Factory. "We appreciate the continued support of Mitsubishi HC Capital as we scale our operations."

Sustainability: Become a market leader in sustainability.

  • The Company continued to compost 100% of its food waste and donate 100% of its produce extras.
  • The Company's Bolingbrook facility operates on the high-efficiency HVAC units installed during the buildout, reducing energy consumption and supporting the Company's commitment to lowering operational emissions.

Q3 2026 covers the thirteen- and thirty-nine-week periods ending October 3, 2026, compared to the three- and nine-month periods ending September 30, 2025, for Q3 2025, following the Company's adoption of a 4-4-5 fiscal calendar in 2026 to better align internal management reporting and operations. As a result, certain financial results for individual reporting periods may not be directly comparable to prior periods.

This earnings news release should be read in conjunction with the Company's interim financial statements for the thirteen and thirty-nine weeks ending October 3, 2026 (the "Interim Financial Statements"), and the related Management's Discussion and Analysis (the "MD&A"); both documents are available to download on The Fresh Factory's profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca.

For conversion purposes, this release used $0.70 as the conversion rate from CAD to USD.

All figures in this news release are in US dollars unless otherwise stated.

About The Fresh Factory B.C. Ltd.

The Fresh Factory is a vertically integrated company focused on accelerating the growth of the fresh, clean-label, and better-for-you food and beverage brands of tomorrow. The Fresh Factory owns or partners with emerging brands in the better-for-you space to develop, manufacture, and sell products made from fresh produce and recognizable ingredients. It operates from two manufacturing facilities near Chicago, serving customers across the United States. As a public benefit corporation, The Fresh Factory is ESG-focused, driven to make a lighter, greener impact on the environment and a stronger, positive impact on local communities and the food system as a whole. Learn more about The Fresh Factory at www.thefreshfactory.co and find The Fresh Factory on social media at Instagram, X, and LinkedIn.

There are measures included in this news release that do not have a standardized meaning under international financial reporting standards (IFRS) and therefore, may not be comparable to similarly titled measures and metrics presented by other publicly traded companies. The Company includes these measures because it believes certain investors use them as a means of assessing financial performance. Billed revenue, adjusted gross margin, operating profit, EBITDA, and adjusted EBITDA are financial measures that do not have a standardized meaning under IFRS. EBITDA is defined as earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization. Adjusted EBITDA refers to earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, amortization, costs of being public, share-based compensation, and one-time transaction expenses. Adjusted gross margin is defined as billed revenue minus food, packaging, and labor (i.e., COGs). Operating profit is adjusted gross margin less utilities, facilities, and maintenance costs. Billed revenue is a financial measure defined as the revenue billed to customers as opposed to total revenue, which represents billed revenue less trade and variable selling and any production credits and samples.

We prepare and release quarterly unaudited and annual audited financial statements prepared in accordance with IFRS. data.title: Frontier Nuclear Receives Nasdaq Notification Regarding Minimum Bid Price Deficiency
data.description:
Winnipeg, Manitoba--(Newsfile Corp. - November 27, 2026) - Frontier Nuclear and Minerals Inc. ("Frontier"), a nuclear fuel cycle company, announces that on November 25, 2026, it received a written notification letter (the "Notification Letter") from the Nasdaq Stock Market LLC ("Nasdaq"), notifying Frontier that it was not in compliance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2), as the minimum bid price of Frontier's common shares ("Shares") has been below US $1.00 per share for 30 consecutive business days.

The Notification Letter is only a notification of deficiency and not a notice of delisting. As such, the Notification Letter has no immediate effect on the listing or trading of Frontier's Shares on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the symbol "FNUC."

Nasdaq Listing Rules

Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2) requires securities listed on the Nasdaq Capital Market to maintain a minimum bid price of US$1.00 per share, and Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(A) provides that a failure to meet the minimum bid price requirement exists if the deficiency continues for a period of 30 consecutive business days. Based on the closing bid price of Frontier's Shares for the 30 consecutive business days from October 14, 2026 to November 24, 2026, Frontier has not met the minimum bid price requirement.

In accordance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(A), Frontier has a period of 180 calendar days, or until May 24, 2027 in which to regain compliance with the minimum bid price requirement. To regain compliance, the closing bid price of the Frontier's Shares must meet or exceed US $1.00 for at least ten consecutive business days during this 180-calendar day period. In the event Frontier does not regain compliance by May 24, 2027, Frontier may be eligible for an additional 180 calendar day grace period if it meets the continued listing requirement for market value of publicly held shares (US $1 million) and all other initial listing standards for The Nasdaq Capital Market, with the exception of the bid price and provides written notice to Nasdaq of its intention to cure the deficiency during the second compliance period, by effecting a reverse stock split, if necessary. If it appears to Nasdaq that Frontier will not be able to cure the deficiency, or if Frontier is not otherwise eligible for additional time to regain compliance, Frontier's Shares will be subject to delisting by Nasdaq. Frontier may still appeal Nasdaq's determination to delist its Shares, and during any appeal process, Frontier's Shares would continue to trade on the Nasdaq Capital Market.

Frontier is issuing this press release pursuant to Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(b). Nasdaq advised Frontier that it will be added to Nasdaq's public list of non-compliant companies beginning five business days after the date of the notice. Nasdaq will also distribute a non-compliance indicator through its market data network and make it available to third-party market data providers.

Frontier's management intends to actively monitor the bid price for its Shares and will consider all available options to regain compliance with the Nasdaq minimum bid price requirement.

Frontier's business operations are not affected by the receipt of the Notification Letter.

About Frontier Nuclear and Minerals Inc.

Frontier Nuclear and Minerals Inc. is focused on building a U.S.-based nuclear fuel cycle platform through uranium exploration and development assets, together with targeted investments in Ubaryon Pty. Ltd., a private Australian company developing next generation enrichment technology, and Kadmos Energy Services LLC, a private U.S. company developing small modular light water reactors. Frontier continues to evaluate opportunities in the nuclear fuel cycle that align with its long-term strategic objectives.

For more information, visit: www.frontiernuclear.com

data.description:
Brisbane, Australia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 27, 2026) - Adyton Resources Corporation (OTCQB: ADYRF) (FSE: 701) ("Adyton" or the "Company") announces that it has filed its financial statements for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and accompanying Management Discussion and Analysis on its SEDAR+ profile at www.sedarplus.ca.

KEY HIGHLIGHTS

  • Fiscal discipline and strong quarter-end cash position:The Company maintained a disciplined approach to capital allocation throughout the year, ensuring efficient deployment of funds across exploration programs. As a result, the Company ended the period with a combined cash and cash equivalents and other financial assets (Term Deposits) of $11.2 million at September 30, 2026, providing a strong foundation for planned activities in the upcoming period.
  • Mining lease granted for Fergusson Wapolu project:On November 17, 2026, the Company received formal notification that the Mineral Resources Authority in Papua New Guinea granted Mining Lease ML 1390 ("ML") and Lease for Mining Purposes LMP ("LMP") 152 to Fergusson Wapolu Limited in respect of the Wapolu Gold Project on Fergusson Island.ML 1390 covers an area of approximately 845.54 hectares and has a term of 20 years, while LMP 152 covers approximately 95.40 hectares and has a term of five years. Both tenements are effective November 12, 2026.The granting of these tenements represents a major regulatory milestone in the Company's strategy to advance the Wapolu Gold Project toward commercial production. The Mining Lease provides the principal mineral tenure required for mining activities, while the Lease for Mining Purposes supports associated mining infrastructure and development activities, subject to applicable conditions and regulatory requirements.The Company is progressing the administrative requirements associated with the grants and will continue to advance processing plant commissioning, mine development planning and other operational preparations.Although the grants represent a significant step toward the recommencement of mining operations at Wapolu, the timing of commercial production remains subject to the satisfaction of applicable regulatory conditions, completion of commissioning and other operational requirements.
  • Adyton commences trading on the Papua New Guinea Stock Exchange:The Company commenced trading on the Papua New Guinea Stock Exchange, under the symbol "ADY", complementing its primary listing on the TSX Venture Exchange in Canada and providing Papua New Guinean investors with a direct domestic market through which to gain exposure to the Company and its portfolio of gold and copper-gold projects in Papua New Guinea.
  • Updated Mineral Resource Estimate for the Fergusson Gameta Project:As indicated in the previous quarter, the Company reported an updated NI 43 101 Mineral Resource Estimate (MRE) for its Gameta Gold Project ("Gameta") on Fergusson Island, Papua New Guinea (PNG).The updated Gameta MRE incorporates approximately 4,000 metres of infill drilling completed in 2025 and comprises an indicated mineral resource of 8.94 million tonnes grading 1.41g/t Au containing 404,000 ounces of gold and an inferred mineral resource of 6.52 million tonnes grading 0.99g/t Au containing 207,000 ounces of gold. The estimate was prepared by Mining One under the authorship of Louis Cohalan (MAIG), an independent mining consultant ‎and "qualified person" as defined in NI 43-101.

data.title: Glass Lewis backs Vail Resorts board in proxy fight with activist Oasis
data.description:
Key points:
  • Glass Lewis backs nine Vail directors before December 14 vote
  • Oasis seeks to elect Bob Chapek, Ashton Hudson to board
  • Glass Lewis raised concerns about Chapek's financial arrangement with Oasis

By Svea Herbst-Bayliss

Proxy advisory firm Glass Lewis urged Vail Resorts investors to reelect the mountain resort operator's directors, arguing the three dissident candidates are not qualified to sit on the board or are too financially tied to hedge fund Oasis Management.

Glass Lewis, one of the two leading US firms that guide investor voting on issues such as board elections ‌and ​corporate mergers, backed the company's nine directors in one of the season's most hotly contested fights before the December 14 vote. The Glass Lewis report was seen by Reuters on Friday.

Proxy advisory firm Egan-Jones earlier recommended investors elect all of Vail's director candidates. Institutional Shareholder Services, the biggest proxy advisory firm, has not yet issued its recommendation.

Oasis Management, Vail's fourth-largest investor with a 9.6% stake, is urging investors to elect its two proposed directors, former Walt Disney CEO Bob Chapek and Ashton Hudson, who has served on various boards.

Gregory Meyer, an independent shareholder, wants shareholders to elect him to the board. Both Oasis and Meyer have criticized the company's financial performance and stock price, which has tumbled more than 57% in the last five years, even though it has gained 7% since January. Vail's stock closed at $143.07 on Friday, leaving it with a market value of $5.1 billion.

"Coming off a weather-wracked fiscal year punctuated by the sudden return of (CEO Rob) Katz, Vail has bolstered its board and executive bench and launched a series of tactical initiatives which appear closely tuned to both the Company's legacy failings and investor feedback derived from extended engagement," Glass Lewis wrote.

The report criticized the dissident candidates. "The establishment of singular compensatory arrangements with Mr. Chapek, a nominee intended to be independent of Oasis — runs counter to sound governance," the report said.

Glass Lewis cited Oasis' compensation to Chapek, saying it was structured "in exceptionally atypical fashion." Oasis said in a regulatory filing in October that it is paying Chapek $100,000 per month in consulting fees and extending a $500,000 forgivable loan, to be used to purchase Vail common stock if Chapek is elected.

"The remaining nominees — M. Ashton Hudson on the one hand, Gregory Meyer on the other — do not clearly offer experience and expertise more effectively aligned with Vail's current strategic trajectory," the report added.

Neither Meyer nor Oasis was immediately available for comment.

data.title: Scott Aaronson says AI labs may hold unreleased math results that could weaken RSA
data.description:
For years, the big threat to RSA encryption had a familiar face: a sufficiently powerful quantum computer. Scott Aaronson is now suggesting the first crack could come from somewhere else entirely.

Aaronson is a computer science professor at the University of Texas at Austin and previously worked as a researcher at OpenAI. He says AI labs may be holding undisclosed mathematical breakthroughs that could weaken RSA before quantum machines ever show up to do the job.

On November 25, 2026, Aaronson said he is "virtually certain, from multiple reliable sources" that leading AI labs have cryptography results they have not made public. He named OpenAI and Anthropic specifically.

He said these labs could hold results or algorithms capable of undermining current cryptographic standards. The operative word is "could." Nobody outside those labs has seen the work, and Aaronson did not claim to have seen it either.

He was also careful to separate his claim from the louder version circulating online. Since mid-November 2026, rumors have spread that an AI lab has produced a polynomial-time integer factoring algorithm.

That phrase needs some unpacking. RSA's security depends on the fact that splitting a very large number into its prime factors is brutally hard for ordinary computers. A polynomial-time algorithm would make that task scale manageably as numbers grow, turning a near-impossible job into a merely tedious one.

Aaronson said he has encountered no verified evidence supporting that rumor. So his position is roughly this: labs probably have cryptography results sitting in a drawer, but the specific doomsday story going viral has not been substantiated.

The companies themselves have stayed quiet. As of November 27, 2026, neither OpenAI nor Anthropic had issued any public statement confirming a cryptography breakthrough.

Aaronson has been tracking AI's effect on mathematics for years. On October 7, 2026, he noted that AI companies were privately testing their models against cryptographic protocols.

He also pointed out a conspicuous gap. The recent wave of AI-generated math publications has delivered notable results across various fields, yet cryptographic results have been absent from those releases.

Around November 25, 2026, Google released a paper presenting a new factoring algorithm. It was regarded as theoretically interesting but not practical for breaking RSA.

He also drew a line between intellectual progress in mathematics and practical consequences for security. A clever new result about numbers does not automatically translate into an attack that works against deployed systems.

All of this lands while the security community is already preparing for a different threat. Post-quantum cryptography is the ongoing effort to build encryption that can withstand both classical computers and future quantum machines.

Aaronson's comments introduce a second variable: AI-assisted mathematics could chip away at classical assumptions on its own schedule. A threat that might emerge quietly from a private lab is much harder to plan around than quantum hardware that can be watched developing in public.

For now, the honest status is unconfirmed. A credible researcher has expressed confidence about undisclosed work, an unverified rumor is circulating that he explicitly declined to endorse, and the two labs he named have said nothing.

If AI labs are generating cryptography results and choosing not to publish them, that raises questions about disclosure. Security research has traditionally depended on findings being shared so defenders can respond.

The things to watch are fairly concrete. First, whether OpenAI or Anthropic says anything publicly about cryptography research, in either direction. Second, whether any AI-assisted cryptography results appear in published work, where outside experts can check them. Third, whether follow-up analysis of Google's factoring paper changes the assessment that it is impractical against RSA. And finally, whether Aaronson himself adds detail, since his comments are currently the main anchor for this whole conversation.

The encryption protecting much of the internet has not been shown to be broken. But one of the people best placed to judge the question thinks the labs know more than they are saying.
